npm run lint -w apps/bot: PASS, clean (`> bot@0.1.0 lint` / `> eslint .`, zero errors/warnings, no output). npm run build -w apps/bot: PASS, clean (`> bot@0.1.0 build` / `> tsc -p tsconfig.json`, zero errors, no output).

Postgres (bot-postgres-1) was already running (3h uptime) from the prior baseline run -- confirmed via `docker compose ps`, no restart needed.

Ran `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` from the repo root TWICE (DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot): attempt 1 = 44 passed (44 files), 405 passed (405 tests), 56.88s. Attempt 2 = 44 passed (44 files), 405 passed (405 tests), 55.31s. Both attempts fully clean -- zero failures, including AC8's previously-failing first it(), which now passes in both runs.

Ran the AC4 concurrency block in isolation a third time (`npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCodeRedeem.db.test.ts -t AC4 --reporter=verbose`): both cases PASSED -- literal-shape case (20 iterations, two concurrent redeemers) in 773ms, higher-fan-in case (5 iterations x 10 concurrent redeemers, dedicated pool with totalCount evidence of real multi-connection parallelism) in 521ms. Combined with both full-suite runs (where these same two cases also passed), AC4's concurrency property is confirmed stable across three independent executions in this rework re-verification, with zero flakiness observed -- consistent with the 3/3 stability already established in the prior baseline run before this rework touched anything.

Verified AC8's fix directly in the committed test file (not just relying on TEST-DESIGNER's description): apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCodeRedeem.db.test.ts's AC8 first it() now builds `normalizedDesignText = designText.replace(/\s+/g, " ")` and runs both toContain checks against the normalized text. Both required phrases -- "resolution (a): the rule applies uniformly to every" and "No column is added to `events`" -- are still asserted in full, so the fix removes the line-wrap fragility without weakening what AC8 verifies. Spot-checked docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-038.md's File 1 fenced source against the committed test file around the AC8 block: consistent with TEST-DESIGNER's rework1 claim of byte-for-byte sync.

No other test case, file, or count changed versus the prior baseline run (test-reports/report-2026-09-08-WF02-REQ-038.yaml) apart from AC8's first it() flipping from FAIL to PASS -- exactly the outcome TEST-DESIGNER's rework1 targeted, no coverage gained or lost.

Committed this handoff and the new test report (test-reports/report-2026-09-08-WF02-REQ-038-rework1.yaml) to feature/WF02-REQ-038 and pushed. `git status` confirmed clean after the commit.
